messages.content: Write a nomination for an internal engineering award, for a team that improved the deployment process. Around 200 words.

output:
**Nomination — [Award name]: [Team name]**

Eighteen months ago, a production release meant a 40-step runbook, a two-hour maintenance window, and someone on the team giving up their evening. Rollbacks were a phone tree. Most of us treated Friday as unshippable.

[Team] rebuilt that. They replaced the runbook with a pipeline, added staged rollouts with automatic health gates, and made rollback a single command that finishes in under a minute. None of this arrived as a big-bang rewrite. They migrated one service at a time, sat with each owning team during their first few deploys, and fixed the rough edges before moving on.

The numbers: median time from merge to production dropped from [X] to [Y]. Change failure rate fell by [Z]%. Deploy volume roughly tripled, and off-hours pages tied to releases are close to zero.

What I want to highlight is the part that doesn't show up in a dashboard. Engineers outside their team now ship small changes without ceremony, because the cost of being wrong got low enough to stop worrying about. [Team] took work nobody finds glamorous and made everyone else's job easier. That deserves recognition.

Nominated by [Your name], [Team/Org].

Send me the team name, the real metrics, and one specific incident or migration you want called out, and I'll tighten it around those.
